transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! It's nice to speak with you. I'm Dora, and I'm here to help with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, yes, I have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start doing light gardening activities, such as brisk walking, gardening, and gentle cycling, about 1 week after your surgery. However, it's best to avoid heavy lifting, bending, or strenuous exercise for a month. If you're planning to do any gardening, just be sure to take it easy and not overexert yourself. Also, remember to avoid getting water in your eyes, especially in the first month after surgery.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, that makes sense. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use the preservative-free eye drops as prescribed. If you're running low, you can get more from your GP. Just make sure to use them four times a day as directed.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, thank you for letting me know. Another thing I was wondering about is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal to be a bit sensitive to light after cataract surgery, especially in bright sunlight. Mild sensitivity is okay, and you can try wearing sunglasses when you're outside. However, if you're experiencing significant pain or discomfort when it's bright, or if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess it further.
